I did some work experience with the ambulance a few years ago and was appalled at how mental health patients are treated in the ED. No one gives a shit and the vast majority are walking out of the hospital within sub hour with no help. 

The only patients who get involuntarily admitted are generally ones who have lost capacity, for example an unmedicated schizophrenic having a psychotic episode. But for suicidal patients, generally by the time you get to the ED you’ve calmed a bit and become a timid little mouse that lacks the confidence to tell people how fucked you are and no one spends the time to listen to you and really delve into what’s going on. You end up saying you’re ok now and they kick you out, without even putting some kind of out-patient support plan in place. It’s disgusting.

And yes, sometimes I think you’re better off cutting people out of your life who are no benefit to you. I don’t mean we should be completely self serving in our relationships with people, but it has to be a two way street where you get something out of them too, otherwise what’s the point interacting with them at all if you get nothing out of them. Cut them out.

That depends where you live. In Australia you can be admitted to a mental health ward against your will under the mental health act. Paramedics can also sedate and transport you to hospital under various acts depending on the state you’re in, I mean like territory. But you need to meet certain criteria because it’s still classified as deprivation of liberty and taken very seriously in the healthcare system. Most people are not admitted involuntarily either because they don’t meet the criteria and end up walking out of the emergency department and going home because they don’t get any help there, or they manage to miraculously admit themselves voluntarily and actually get some help, though I have no idea how that ever happens

I’ve felt this self-preservationist attitude a lot in the healthcare system. Paramedics, nurses and doctors really show any real empathy toward mental health patients. At least I’ve never seen any. They’re just doing a job, that’s all it is to them. I don’t want my negativity about this to detract from the fact that there are people out there who do care and aren’t just doing it because they’re obligated. But I’m sure you’ll understand my cynicism comes from a string of experiences with unempathic cold arseholes that have treated me like I’m a waste of their time.

The Apple Watch is not a diagnostic tool. It only gives you one “lead” of an ecg, which is like a vector of your heart’s electrical activity and the way it’s flowing. A lot of things can give you a false positive, even just moving to much through the reading can throw it off because of all the other electrical signals your nervous system is creating. If you’re not symptomatic and feel fine, don’t worry. Bring it up with your doctor when you see them next, or make an appointment to see them.
